subject: pe
title: Fitness & Training: Components
welcome_lead: Fitness comes in flavours — cardio, strength, flexibility and more.
meta_desc: KS3 PE: components of fitness, why each matters.
final_note: Train all the parts and you become a complete athlete.

concepts.def: How long heart and lungs can keep going.
How much force a muscle can produce.
How well body parts work together.

walkthroughs.body_html: Cardio endurance is your heart and lungs keeping you going. Running, swimming and cycling build it.
Strength is heavy force; power is strength used fast. A long jump needs both.
Flexibility means joints can move freely. Stretching after exercise keeps muscles long and helps recovery.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between aerobic and muscular endurance?
options: Aerobic is for legs, muscular for arms.
They are different names for the same component.
Aerobic endurance is the cardiovascular system's ability to supply oxygen; muscular endurance is a muscle's ability to contract repeatedly without fatigue.
Gradually increasing training demands so the body keeps adapting.
Training as hard as possible immediately.
Aerobic is for legs, muscular for arms.
The volume of blood in the heart at any moment.
Volume of blood pumped by the heart per minute (stroke volume x heart rate).
